settlement_calendar.basis: Observed RBI auction dates and issue/settlement dates reconciled against weekends plus captured official Mumbai holidays; not a future settlement guarantee.

retail_direct_rules.minimum_rule_source_date: 2021-11-12 circular; RBI FAQ displays minimums as of 2021-11-12
retail_direct_rules.retail_ncb_aggregate_limit: up to 5% of notified nominal issue amount, within notified amount, or other percentage set by RBI; not an individual guaranteed allocation
retail_direct_rules.partial_allotment: pro-rata if auction allocation is partial; actual investor allocation is unknown without bid/allotment records
retail_direct_rules.investor_access: RBI Retail Direct permits eligible individuals to bid in primary T-bill auctions through the non-competitive segment; this capture does not verify this investor's RDG account or operational eligibility
retail_direct_rules.upfront_markup_amount: required by FAQ as part of funding basis, but amount/formula is not specified in captured FAQ; affordability is not qualified
retail_direct_rules.cash_costs: RBI reports no account maintenance or primary bid fee; payment-gateway charges are borne by investor and amount is not specified
retail_direct_rules.settlement: typically one working day after auction; use observed issue dates as historical settlement dates; this is not a guarantee for future auctions

conditional_gross_price_to_par_holding_r.definition: 100 / RBI non-competitive weighted-average price per 100 face - 1; assumes full allotment, hold to redemption at par, and excludes tax, fees, and investor-specific execution.

conditional_365d_target_roll_scenario.lot_rounding: buy the greatest whole number of ₹10,000 face-value lots supported by cash at each observed NCB weighted-average price; upfront markup and payment-gateway charges are excluded, so bid affordability is not established
conditional_365d_target_roll_scenario.next_bid_date_rule: first observed positive 91-day auction date strictly after adjusted maturity; same-day funding is excluded because RBI requires funding on the bid-submission date and intraday maturity-credit timing is not established
conditional_365d_target_roll_scenario.cash_wait_return_assumption: 0% between maturity receipt and next eligible auction; no return is credited while auction funds are reserved or excess markup is awaiting refund
conditional_365d_target_roll_scenario.upfront_markup_and_refund_timing: RBI FAQ requires markup-funded bids and says excess is refunded within two business days; the markup amount is unspecified and not modeled
conditional_365d_target_roll_scenario.overlap_warning: Start cohorts overlap in time and are not independent observations; these descriptive values do not estimate a long-run return distribution or probability.

nominal_roll_schedule_diagnostic.definition: Issue date + 91 calendar days; move maturity backward over weekends and official Mumbai holidays; then select the first positive auction date strictly after adjusted maturity because retail funding is required on the auction/bid date.
limitations: The diagnostic applies RBI's previous-working-day rule using the captured Mumbai matrix and the official rule that the Government securities market is closed on Saturdays; each security's specific maturity terms still require confirmation.

The deterministic one-year-target roll scenario uses the public ₹10,000 minimum lot and historical auction dates, assumes full allotment, and excludes required upfront markup; it does not prove investor-specific access or bid affordability.
The bid-date rule conservatively excludes an auction on the same date as maturity because the exact order of maturity credit and bid-funding cutoff is not established by public evidence.
Actual partial allocation, payment-gateway charges, markup amount/refund cash timing, tax, and any bank cash yield are not modeled.
The two-year observed window is not a long-run interest-rate model or a 2036 probability estimate.
